source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: That the ‘former-N’ (‘ruin’) reading in (123b) arises out of the configuration like the one in (122) where AP modifies N(P) explains the contrast in (124) where bili ‘that’ realizes the DP-layer (repeated from section 3.3). In (124a) the adjective has attached to the noun whose discourse reference has not yet been fixed and therefore the N-modifying ‘ruin’-reading is available. In (124b) the adjective has attached to the DP which rules out the ‘ruin’-reading because the DP’s reference has already been fixed as ‘that house’. On the contrary, urukku ‘old style’ is not restricted in this way and can modify both N or DP.
en: (a) I saw that old style house. (b) I saw that former house (ruin).
